s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
Irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen on MRI
Expansion of the fallopian canal and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal on CT
Lesion had heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
Specimen consisted of cartilage on gross examination
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and low cellularity on microscopic examination

raw.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
Irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen on MRI
Expansion of the fallopian canal and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal on CT
Lesion had heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
Specimen consisted of cartilage on gross examination
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and low cellularity on microscopic examination

raw.rationale: The patient's 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness, nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal, and imaging findings of an irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen with heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast are consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma. The microscopic examination showing pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, low cellularity, and positive staining for S100 also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: While the gross examination showed a specimen consisting of cartilage, the microscopic examination and clinical presentation are more consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma.

rejected.label: Facial nerve neurofibroma
rejected.why: The patient's lack of other significant medical history and the absence of features suggestive of neurofibromatosis type 1 make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Facial nerve paraganglioma
rejected.why: The imaging findings and microscopic examination do not support a paraganglioma, which would typically show a more vascular lesion with a characteristic 'salt and pepper' appearance on imaging.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's age, clinical presentation, and microscopic examination are not consistent with rhabdomyosarcoma, which is a malignant tumor more commonly seen in children and young adults.
